RECONSTRUCTED TEXT — Open Library search-inside, 2026-09-06
===========================================================
McGRAW-HILL DIRECTORY AND ALMANAC OF CANADA, "POST OFFICES IN CANADA" — the Kanawana entry.

NOT A SCAN. Every item of this series on the Internet Archive is lending-restricted and none has
been read. The heading and the entry below were assembled from overlapping twelve-word windows
returned by https://openlibrary.org/search/inside.json (contract at f_4933). Page images return
HTTP 403 with an HTML body even with the item's own details page as Referer.


THE HEADING, walked word by word to its closing bracket
-------------------------------------------------------

    "POST OFFICES IN CANADA (Sub post offices and closed and renamed post offices appear in
    italics. The correct postal address for each closed post office appears immediately below the
    closed post office name.) During summer months mail is delivered to fishing fleets at sea by CN
    Coastal ..."

The running heads on these pages are "Post Offices | Railway Postal Lines & Districts | Airports",
and the list's own legend includes "(S) Seasonal P.O." — so the volume does distinguish seasonal
offices, and does so with a code Kanawana does not carry here.

RECOVERING THE HEADING WAS THE WHOLE JOB, and p_430 was right to say so. The entry alone —
"Kanawana, PQ, see St-Sauveur-des-Monts, PQ" — is ambiguous. In a gazetteer it would mean "for this
place, look under that one". Under this heading it means Kanawana is in the italicised class and
St-Sauveur-des-Monts is the correct postal address for it.


THE ENTRY
---------

    "... Kanasuta, PQ, see] Arntfield, PQ | ON | Kanata, Ont | O | KANAWANA, PQ, SEE
    ST-SAUVEUR-DES-MONTS, PQ | Kandahar, Sask | S CP | Kane ..."

(The single letters are the list's own service codes, printed in a separate column; they are not
decoded here and none of them is attached to Kanawana in the recovered window.)

Present in: mcgrawhilldirect0000unse (leaf 874) and mcgrawhilldirect0000unse_f4f5 (leaf 882).
Not returned for: mcgrawhilldirect0000unse_v4j7 (leaf 842, which carries the same heading) or
mcgrawhilldirect0000unse_j6s5 (leaf 874). A query that does not return a hit is not evidence of
absence in a corpus where OCR hyphenation defeats phrase matching.


WHAT IT ESTABLISHES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT
-----------------------------------------

ESTABLISHES: a closing bracket. The Canadian Almanac's post-office table still carries Kanawana as
an operating office in two volumes of the 1950s, the later of which prints calendars for 1954 and
1955 (f_4936). This list has it in the italicised class. **The office ended between about 1955 and
the mid-1960s** — the first closing bracket this project has, against an opening bracket of March
1909 to 1911 (f_4944).

DOES NOT ESTABLISH: which of the three. The heading puts sub post offices, closed ones and renamed
ones into the same italics. Kanawana was not renamed — the name is still on the map in the 1981
Atlas of Canada — so it is either closed outright or reduced to a sub post office served from
St-Sauveur. This source cannot tell which, and gives no date, no postmaster and no reason.


THE YEAR OF THE VOLUME — AND WHY IT IS NOT WRITTEN AS 1966
----------------------------------------------------------
The Internet Archive holds FOUR items of this series and catalogues EVERY ONE of them 1966. They
are evidently different printings. No internal year was recovered from any of them; the only dating
evidence found in passing was "Robert L. Hanbidge", Lieutenant Governor of Saskatchewan 1963-70,
which is not close enough.

This project has already been caught twice by this catalogue's series dates: every volume of the
Canadian Almanac and Directory is dated 1848, and the UPU Dictionnaire's supplement of August 1912
is dated 1909 — which, taken at face value, would have put a Kanawana post office in existence
before the YMCA arrived. So the year here is carried as **"a mid-1960s volume catalogued 1966"**,
and the closing bracket is written **"by the mid-1960s"** rather than "by 1966".


ACCESS FAILURE, and what remains the authority
----------------------------------------------
archive.org/download/<id>/page/n<leaf>_w1600.jpg -> HTTP 403 with an HTML body, Referer set.
Library and Archives Canada's Post Offices and Postmasters database gives opening dates, closing
dates and postmasters for every Canadian post office and would answer all of this in one lookup.
It refuses this project at the network gateway (HTTP 403), which is a fact about the gateway.
Tracked as p_428. ROUTES NOT TRIED: a request through a Canadian library or a person with ordinary
browser access; the Postal History Society of Canada's published county lists; BAnQ.
